entries.terminator_note: $E6 is a five-byte F5/F8 dispatch prefix; its $F8 operand jumps to CPU $961A within ID $78, so the pointer-table boundary is the source-span end and no local $F0 terminator is expected.

decoding_notes.actor_packets: Scenario $44 selects animation $5C; F1 byte 5 chooses actor index ((b & $1C) >> 2), low bits become active flags, bytes 1/2 select motion/appearance tables, and bytes 3/4 supply coordinates.
decoding_notes.held_pose: F7 stores its operand as the held descriptor. Motion $A38A applies one zero-delta step before the $A390 hold command.
decoding_notes.palette: The bank-$14 palette resolver returns the ordinary player ID unchanged; the normal-player table uses five-byte stride. Player ID $08 selects $B80C + 5*$08 = $B834.
decoding_notes.route_animation_streams: Raw bank-$14 spans are preserved from the route animation pointer table, using the current pointer to the following pointer as the exclusive boundary; the pointer boundary is authoritative, and streams must not be truncated by scanning for $F0. Ordinary entries in this set end with $F0; $79 contains an earlier $F0 inside an $F1 packet operand. ID $E6 is a five-byte F5/F8 dispatch prefix ending at the $E7 pointer, with its $F8 target at CPU $961A inside the ID $78 span; it does not have a local $F0 terminator. IDs $8F/$4E/$66/$4C/$E6 come from byte-checked scenario records; $78/$79/$90 are selectors observed in the same-input actor writer trace, but their upstream selection conditions remain unresolved.
